extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, licensees, counsel, NRC staff, and members of the public interested in NRC licensing and enforcement proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural requirements in 10 CFR Part 2 governing NRC administrative review of applications, notices (proposed action, hearing, issuance), withdrawal/denial, renewal effects, treatment of design/site submittals, anti-discrimination, and procedures for notices of violation and orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review — staff requests and conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: During review of an application by the NRC staff, an applicant may be required to supply additional information. The staff may request any one party to the proceeding to confer with the NRC staff informally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For docketed applications for limited work authorization, construction permit, operating license, early site permit, standard design approval, combined license, or manufacturing license, the NRC staff shall establish a schedule for its review specifying the key intermediate steps from docketing until completion of review. (§ 2.102(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: ACRS referral and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director, Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation, or Director, Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards, as appropriate, will refer the docketed application to the ACRS as required by law and in such additional cases as the Director or the Commission may determine to be appropriate. The ACRS will render to the Commission one or more reports as required by law or as requested by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ACRS report must be made part of the record of the docketed application and copies transmitted to appropriate State and local officials. (§§ 2.102(b)–(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance criteria and notification on issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director finds that an application for a byproduct, source, special nuclear material, facility, or operator license complies with the requirements of the Act, the Energy Reorganization Act, and this chapter, the Director will issue a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the license is for a facility or certain waste or HLW-related authorizations, the Director will inform the State, Tribal and local officials specified in § 2.104(c) of the issuance. (§ 2.103(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed denial or denial — required notice to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director finds that an application does not comply with the requirements of the Act and this chapter the Director may issue a notice of proposed denial or a notice of denial of the application and inform the applicant in writing of:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must state (1) the nature of any deficiencies or the reason for the proposed denial or the denial, and (2) the right of the applicant to demand a hearing within twenty (20) days from the date of the notice or such longer period as may be specified in the notice. (§ 2.103(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing — publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where a hearing is required by the Act or this chapter, or the Commission finds a hearing is required in the public interest, the Secretary will issue a notice of hearing to be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be published at least 15 days before the date set for hearing, and for applications concerning certain facility types (limited work authorization, construction permit, early site permit, combined license for types described in § 50.21(b) or § 50.22 or subpart H of part 53, or a testing facility) at least 30 days before the date set for hearing. If the initial notice does not specify time and place of initial hearing, a subsequent notice providing at least 30-day notice of time and place is required. (§ 2.104(a) and footnote)

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of hearing must state:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) The nature of the hearing; (2) The authority under which the hearing is to be held; (3) The matters of fact and law to be considered; (4) The date by which requests for hearing or petitions to intervene must be filed; (5) The presiding officer designated for the hearing, or the procedure the Commission will use to designate a presiding officer. (§ 2.104(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing — transmission to State/Local/Tribal officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will transmit a notice of hearing on applications for specified licenses (production/utilization facility, limited work authorization, early site permit, combined license, certain waste licenses, part 72 acquisitions, etc.) to the governor or other appropriate official of the State and to the chief executive of the municipality or county (or Tribal organization) in which the facility is to be located or activity conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For part 72 applications to acquire/receive/possess spent fuel or HLW for storage in an MRS, the Secretary will transmit to the same persons who received the notice of docketing under § 72.16(e). (§ 2.104(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: When notice of proposed action or intended operation is required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hearing is not required and the Commission has not found a hearing in the public interest, the Commission will, before acting, publish either a notice of intended operation or a notice of proposed action with respect to applications for:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated items include: (1) license for a facility; (2) license for receipt of waste for commercial disposal (all part 61 licenses); (3) amendments involving significant hazards consideration; (4) specified amendments to operating/combined/manufacturing licenses for certain facility types and testing facilities; (5–8) various high-level waste and geologic repository authorizations and amendments affecting health and safety; (9) any other license or amendment the Commission deems should have an opportunity for public hearing; (10–13) additional specified licenses/amendments (see § 2.105(a)(1)–(13) for full list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed action — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of proposed action published in the Federal Register will set forth:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) The nature of the action proposed; (2) The manner in which a copy of the safety analysis and of the ACRS report, if any, may be obtained or examined. For a notice of intended operation (§ 52.103(a) or § 53.1452(a)), it must also include identification of the NRC action as making the finding required under § 52.103(g) or § 53.1452(g); how licensee notifications and safety analysis copies may be obtained; and any conditions, limitations, or restrictions to be placed on the license and their expiration or removal circumstances. (§ 2.105(b) and (b)(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed action — possible immediate issuance and procedural effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is complete enough to permit all evaluations necessary for issuance of a construction permit and operating license (other than completion inspection), the notice of proposed issuance of a construction permit may provide that on completion of construction and inspection the operating license will be issued without further prior notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice of proposed action will also state that, within the time period provided under § 2.309(b), the applicant may file a request for hearing and any person whose interest may be affected may file a request for hearing or a petition to intervene if a hearing has already been requested. If no request/petition is filed within the prescribed time, the Director may take the proposed action and publish a notice of issuance; if a request/petition is filed, the presiding officer will rule and the Secretary or presiding officer will issue a notice of hearing or appropriate order. (§ 2.105(c)–(e))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of issuance — publication and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director (Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation or Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards) will inform the State/local officials specified in § 2.104(c) and publish in the Federal Register a document announcing the issuance of:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items include a license or amendment for which a notice of proposed action was published; certain amendments whether or not a notice was previously published; and findings under § 52.103(g) or § 53.1452(g). The notice of issuance will set forth: (1) In the case of a license or amendment: (i) the nature of the license or amendment; (ii) how copies of the safety analysis may be obtained/examined; (iii) a finding that the application complies with the Act and this chapter. (2) In the case of a finding under § 52.103(g) or § 53.1452(g): (i) how safety analysis copies may be obtained; (ii) a finding that prescribed inspections/tests/analyses were performed and acceptance criteria met. (§ 2.106(a)–(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application — timing and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may permit an applicant to withdraw an application prior to issuance of a notice of hearing on such terms and conditions as it may prescribe, or may, on receiving a request for withdrawal, deny the application or dismiss it with prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawn prior to issuance of a notice of hearing, the Commission shall dismiss the proceeding. Withdrawal after issuance of a notice of hearing shall be on such terms as the presiding officer may prescribe. Withdrawal does not authorize removal of any document from Commission files. The Director will publish in the Federal Register a notice of withdrawal if notice of receipt of the application was previously published. (§ 2.107(a)–(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of application for failure to supply information — timing and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may deny an application if an applicant fails to respond to a request for additional information within thirty (30) days from the date of the request, or within such other time as may be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will publish in the Federal Register a notice of denial when notice of receipt was previously published but notice of hearing has not yet been published; that notice will provide that, within thirty (30) days after publication, the applicant may demand a hearing and any person whose interest may be affected may file a petition for leave to intervene. When both notice of receipt and notice of hearing have been published, the presiding officer will rule whether an application should be denied under this paragraph. (§ 2.108(a)–(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely renewal application — filing timeframes that preserve license
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain specified renewals, if at least 30 days before expiration of an existing license authorizing continuing activities, the licensee files an application for renewal or for a new license, the existing license will not be deemed to have expired until the application has been finally determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified exceptions set longer minimum filing times: e.g., nuclear power plant licensed under § 50.21(b)/§ 50.22/subpart H of part 53 — sufficient application filed at least 5 years before expiration; early site permit holders — sufficient application at least 12 months before expiration; manufacturing license under subpart F of part 52 or subpart H of part 53 — 12 months; ISFSI under subpart C of part 72 — 2 years; non-power production/utilization facility under § 50.22 or testing facility — 2 years. (§ 2.109(a)–(f))

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and administrative action on standard design approval or early site suitability submittals
rubrics_metrics.description: A submittal for a standard design approval under subpart E of part 52 or under subpart H of part 53 shall be subject to §§ 2.101(a) and 2.390 to the same extent as if it were an application for a permit or license. A submittal for early review of site suitability issues under appendix Q to parts 50 shall be subject to §§ 2.101(a)(2)–(4) to the same extent as if it were an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon initiation of review the Director shall publish a notice of receipt in the Federal Register inviting comments from interested persons within 60 days (or other time specified) for consideration by NRC staff and ACRS. Upon completion of review of a standard design approval, the Director shall publish a determination as to acceptability (subject to terms and conditions) and make available a report analyzing the design. Upon completion of early site suitability review, the NRC staff shall prepare a staff site report stating location, issues reviewed, scope/nature of review, conclusions and reasons; publish notice of availability and make the report available on NRC Web site and send copies to Governor and local chief executives. (§ 2.110(a)–(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of sex discrimination in NRC programs
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall on the grounds of sex be excluded from participation in, be denied a license, standard design approval, or petition for rulemaking (including a design certification), be denied the benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity carried on or receiving Federal assistance under the Act or the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit nondiscrimination requirement applicable to programs and activities under the Act. (§ 2.111)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of subpart B — proceedings to impose requirements, modify/suspend/revoke licenses, civil penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart prescribes the procedures in cases initiated by the staff, or upon a request by any person, to impose requirements by order, or to modify, suspend, or revoke a license, or to take other action as may be proper, against any person subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It also prescribes procedures for staff-initiated civil penalties pursuant to section 234 of the Act and section 206 of the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974, with special rules for holders of part 76 certificates. (§ 2.200)

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of violation — content and required response
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to an alleged violation, the Commission may serve a written notice of violation which will concisely state the alleged violation and may require that the licensee or other person submit, within 20 days of the date of the notice or other specified time, a written explanation or statement in reply including:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required matter in reply may include: (1) Corrective steps taken and results achieved; (2) Corrective steps which will be taken; (3) The date when full compliance will be achieved. The notice may require admission/denial of the violation and state reasons. If an adequate reply is not received within the specified time, the Commission may issue an order or demand for information as to why the license should not be modified, suspended, or revoked or why other action should not be taken. (§ 2.201(a)–(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders — allegations, required contents, and initial procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may institute a proceeding to modify, suspend, or revoke a license by serving an order that will: (1) Alleged the violations or potentially hazardous conditions and specify the action proposed; (2) Require the licensee to file a written answer under oath or affirmation within twenty (20) days (or other specified time); (3) Inform the recipient of their right, within twenty (20) days (or other specified time), to demand a hearing on all or part of the order; (4) State that requests for hearing by other adversely affected persons must be made within twenty (20) days and meet § 2.309 requirements; (5) Specify the issues for hearing; and (6) State the effective date of the order, which may be immediately effective if public health, safety or interest requires or if violation is willful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A licensee must respond by filing a written answer under oath/affirmation, specifically admitting or denying each allegation and setting forth matters of fact and law relied upon; unless consented, the answer may demand a hearing. (§ 2.202(a)–(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness of orders — motions, live testimony, burdens, and presiding officer timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an order is immediately effective, the licensee may, in addition to demanding a hearing, file a motion to set aside the immediate effectiveness on the ground the order is not based on adequate evidence but on mere suspicion, unfounded allegations, or error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such motion must state particular reasons and be accompanied by affidavits or other evidence. Any party may move for live testimony; presiding officer may order live testimony. NRC staff shall respond in writing within 5 days to motions to set aside immediate effectiveness or to orders denying live testimony; where live testimony is ordered, staff may present live testimony. The presiding officer conducts live testimony under § 2.319 powers (no subpoenas, discovery, referred rulings or certified questions to the Commission). The presiding officer may delay the hearing for good cause consistent with due process. The licensee challenging immediate effectiveness bears the burden of going forward with evidence that the order is not based on adequate evidence; the NRC staff bears the burden of persuading the presiding officer that adequate evidence supports immediate effectiveness. The presiding officer shall issue a decision on the motion expeditiously and may not stay immediate effectiveness during pendency; an order upholding immediate effectiveness constitutes final agency action on immediate effectiveness and will be promptly referred to the Commission. (§ 2.202(c)(i)–(viii))

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to entry of order — waiver and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: An answer may consent to the entry of an order in substantially the form proposed with respect to all or some actions proposed. The consent of the licensee in the answer or other written document to the entry of an order shall constitute a waiver by the licensee of a hearing, findings of fact and conclusions of law, and of all right to seek Commission and judicial review or to contest the validity of the order in any forum as to those matters which have been consented to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An order that has been consented to shall have the same force and effect as an order made after hearing by a presiding officer or the Commission, and shall be effective as provided in the order. (§ 2.202(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders involving backfits or changes to specific licensing categories — follow specified requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the order involves modification of a part 50 or part 53 license and is a backfit, the requirements of § 50.109 or § 53.1590 shall be followed, unless the licensee has consented. If the order involves modification of combined licenses under subpart C of part 52 or subpart H of part 53, the requirements of § 52.98 or § 53.1443 shall be followed unless consented. Similar cross-references apply for early site permit changes, changes to standard design certification rules, standard design approvals, and modification of manufacturing licenses under subpart F of part 52 or subpart H of part 53.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry specifies which other regulatory provisions must be followed for particular categories of changes, unless the applicant or licensee consents to the required action. (§ 2.202(e)(1)–(6))
